text.p: Lebanon's national carrier Middle East Airlines received on Thursday a leased A321 Airbus as part of its programme to rehabilitate and expand.
MEA chairman Khaled Salam who arrived on board the plane coming from Hamburg said another A321 was due to arrive by Tuesday.
"We have finished the first phase which was the leasing of four planes. We hope that they will add to the efficiency of the company operations," Salam told reporters at Beirut airport.
MEA received the two other A320s which it also leased from the U.S./French ILFC company earlier in 1997.

The four planes bring to eight the total number of Airbuses leased by the company. These include two A310-200s which will be returned to KLM as their leases end soon and two A310-300s which will be retained.
In addition, MEA owns three 22-year-old Boeing 747s and seven 707s.
The company has increased its capital and embarked on an ambitious programme to regain its pre-war dominance in the region.
In February, MEA completed the third phase of a capital increase which brought its capital up to $178.75 million. It plans a further increase to reach $225 million by mid-1998.
MEA is 99 percent owned by the Bank of Lebanon, which carried out a $100 million debt-for-equity swap last September that wiped out most of the airline's debts accumulated between 1990 and 1995.
Salam said the company losses had been shrinking lately. Previously, he told Reuters the company was expected to lose $20 million in 1997 and break even in 1998. It lost $50 million in 1996.
